I don't think OpenStreetMap can benefit directly unless the physical location of the cell tower is known (along with more information like operator). More specialized database like opencellid.org are a better fit.

There is at least one OpenStreetMap mobile app (Keypad Mapper on Android) which already allows submitting data to opencellid.org.

Apartment discovery is already well served. There are a dozen new startups that apply innovative methods to search. http://www.apartmentlist.com/, https://livelovely.com/, http://42floors.com/ come to mind.

Software for estate agents needs to be become more modern though. http://nestio.com/ just rebranded themselves to do that for example.

There's a German property portal (number two in the market) which released an iPad app for estate agents. Property management, contact list, calendar etc. Something like 50 USD/month for the app or $100/month for the hardware&app. Website is in German, but there are screenshots and video http://immonetmanager.de/produkt/
How come the special '?utm=hackernews_tarikozket' got added at the end of the URL?

You can. For worldwide coverage you'd need at least 500GB disc space and 2-3 days of data crunching (assuming 32GB RAM, 8 cores, SSDs...) to build the Nominatim database. Photon is using Nominatim's database as input and will take another 2 days (if I remember correctly, met the author last year) to build. (I work on OSM data professionally)
